course.title: Bayesian Modelling and Decisions under Uncertainty
course.tagline: Build Bayesian models of uneven data, prove the computation and the code are sound, and turn the posterior into a decision with a price on further data
course.description: Participants build Bayesian models that support decisions and judge models built by others. On synthetic burst records from 140 districts of a fictional water utility, they test priors by simulation, fit and diagnose Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, pool small districts hierarchically, check and compare models by predictive accuracy, and verify code by simulation-based calibration. The last day turns posteriors into a replacement plan by expected utility and prices a proposed leak survey by its value of information.
course.audience: Specialists. Data scientists who have completed the level 300 core or can show equivalent work: a defended analysis with a validated model or a causal estimate that they can explain.
prerequisites: DS-301 Regression and Generalised Linear Modelling
Fits and interprets generalised linear models in code
Simulates from probability distributions and computes a likelihood
course.format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

outcomes.text: Implement a Bayesian workflow from prior predictive simulation to sampler diagnosis, given a burst-count model with network length as exposure
outcomes.evidence: a notebook with prior draws, diagnostics and a reason for each prior

outcomes.text: Design a hierarchical model for districts with very unequal data and defend the pooling it implies, given 140 districts, a third with fewer than five recorded bursts
outcomes.evidence: no-, complete- and partial-pooling estimates with a written defence

outcomes.text: Evaluate competing models by posterior predictive checks and approximate leave-one-out cross-validation and choose one for the decision, given three candidate models of the same data
outcomes.evidence: a comparison table with check plots and the reasoning

outcomes.text: Diagnose an error in a model implementation by parameter recovery and simulation-based calibration, given a model with a seeded coding error
outcomes.evidence: calibration plots that locate the error and a corrected model that passes

outcomes.text: Decide a replacement plan by expected utility under the posterior and price further data by its value of information, given costs, a capital budget and an offered acoustic leak survey
outcomes.evidence: a two-page memo with the plan, its expected loss and a verdict on the survey

outcomes.text: Review another analyst's Bayesian analysis for priors, computation, checking and reporting, given an analysis with six planted flaws
outcomes.evidence: a review that finds at least four flaws and ranks them by effect on the decision

case_study.name: Yanabi Water Authority
case_study.summary: Yanabi Water Authority is a fictional water utility with 140 districts, from 200 km urban networks to rural networks of one or two kilometres, some with burst sensors and most rural ones without. Participants model five years of synthetic burst records with known generating parameters (seed 401), with planted problems to find: very unequal districts, under-reporting where no sensors listen, extra year-to-year variation, a trunk-main failure year, a seeded coding error and a consultant analysis with six flaws; the posterior then decides a re-piping plan within a capital budget and the price of an acoustic leak survey.
